transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands - January 5, 2026 | Start 10:00 PST | Duration ~72 min
Attendees: Maya (CEO), Jordan (CTO), Priya (VP Product), Liam (Head of Eng), Elena (Head CS), entire company (remote)

[00:00] Maya: Good morning everyone, um, welcome to the January all-hands. Happy new year, first off, thank you all for shipping through a very busy Q4. I want to start with a quick thank you and a couple of high-level numbers.
[00:18] Maya: We finished the year at $38M ARR, which is, uh, higher than our internal plan \u2014 great work. Net retention held at 118% for the quarter, and we closed three Dedicated deals that will start ramping in Jan. Big shout out to sales and solutions.
[00:36] (applause, a few cheery 'woo's in the background)
[00:45] Jordan: Quick tech update from my side \u2014 Private v1 shipped to the first pilot customers in Dec. It's early, there are known gaps (we spelled out a few in the pilot notes), but overall the runtime and orchestration held up under our initial benchmarks. We saw a few KV cache regressions under bursty traffic \u2014 sometimes the telemetry said K V cash instead of K V cache \u2014 so we have a hotfix inbound.
[01:10] Jordan: Also, the new kernel selector updates reduced median token latency by about 15% on our 1k seq workload in the smoke tests. That aligns with our focus on latency-sensitive customers.
[01:27] Priya: From product, Dedicated expansion will include new burst capacity controls and a simplified autoscale policy \u2014 customers asked for easier burst windows rather than fiddly autoscale configs. We'll publish docs next week.
[01:42] Priya: We're also piloting Optimize suggestions as a paid add-on \u2014 it surfaces batching and quantization recommendations per route. Early customers reduced token cost by ~22% in pilots.
[01:55] Liam: Hiring/update \u2014 engineering grew 18 headcount in Q4, we have two open backend+runtime roles and one infra security hire prioritized for Q1. Please use the internal hiring prioritization form if you have role requests.
[02:10] Elena: Customer success highlights \u2014 we had an enterprise win where the customer moved from two self-hosted vendors to Redwood Dedicated after a week-long POC. The deciding factor was our predictable throughput and the observability hooks. They liked the tracing and per-route cost breakdowns.
[02:29] Employee (unlabeled): Question on SLA for Dedicated \u2014 will it be contractual?
[02:33] Priya: Yes, Dedicated will have an SLA option. We're finalizing the SLO targets; Jordan's team is doing the reliability modeling. We'll publish a pricing + SLA sheet by Jan 14.
[02:46] [03:00] Maya: A few customer stories \u2014 one is a healthcare customer that required private deployment w/ HSM integration; Private v1 handled the primary workload but we need to tighten the KMS rotations and provide clearer audit log docs.
[03:18] Maya: On the GTM side, our PLG motion is strong; self-serve signups were up 46% MoM in December (we had a marketing promo), but conversions to paying Dedicated remain the key lever. Sales and Solutions will focus on templated POCs and a faster path to an SLA conversation.
[03:40] Jordan: Quick technical deep-dive summary \u2014 we prioritized three runtime improvements over the break: 1) better KV cache eviction heuristics, 2) kernel dispatcher for quantized models, and 3) improved batching heuristics that avoid latency tail spikes. We pushed a canary to staging last night.
[04:02] Jordan: Note: there was some noisy telemetry for model name mapping in the onboarding path \u2014 some customers saw 'redwood-something' mapped to the wrong variant; that is fixed in the canary.
[04:18] [04:25] Priya: Roadmap prioritization \u2014 our H1 focus is reliability, cost per token improvements, and making Private a smoother experience. Feature-wise: structured streaming outputs, function/tool calling expanded, and better model version pinning in the control plane.
[04:40] Priya: We will deprioritize low-adoption connectors for Q1 to free up cycles for Private/Optimize work.
[04:50] (murmurs of agreement)
[05:00] Employee (Slack question read aloud): "Will there be an engineering freeze for onboarding new models?"
[05:05] Liam: No, not a freeze. We'll be more selective: new model onboardings will go through a short evaluation queue and checklist to avoid surprises in production.
[05:16] [05:30] Maya: On finance \u2014 we're tracking to plan; cash runway extended modestly after the Series C bridge and the Dedicated contracts. We are still investing in R&D, but we want to be prudent.
[05:44] Maya: A quick org note \u2014 we'll centralize platform reliability under a single manager by the end of Jan; that'll help with cross-team SLO ownership.
[05:55] Elena: CS/Support will roll out post-sale playbooks for Dedicated and Private customers so onboarding time is shorter. We'll also publish the audit log and compliance checklist (SOC2 items) in the partner portal.
[06:10] [06:30] Q&A (open floor)
[06:32] Employee A: Any guidance on open-source model strategy? Customers ask about hosting LLMs like LlamaX or other community models.
[06:39] Jordan: We will keep a curated catalog \u2014 the focus is vetted performance profiles. We won't be a dumping ground for fragile community weights; every model must pass a perf and safety bar. That said, we will expand our community model tests and publish verified profiles.
[06:55] Employee B: How do we compare to major public APIs on latency/cost?
[07:00] Priya: Public APIs are competitive on simplicity, but our differentiator is predictable cost and routing policies that trade off latency and throughput. For customers needing single-digit latency, our Dedicated pools or Private (on-prem/VPC) will be the play.
[07:18] [07:30] (Cross talk, someone says 'K8s...' quickly)
[07:33] Jordan: Technical note \u2014 Private v1 currently supports a limited on-prem footprint; full k8s operator will come in v1.1. We heard customers asking for an operator; it's scheduled but not immediate.
[07:47] [08:00] Maya: Hiring priorities \u2014 focus on senior infra and reliability engineers. People Ops, please align with product and eng leads; we'll target closing the critical three hires by end of Q1.
[08:14] [08:30] Priya: On pricing \u2014 we are simplifying the Dedicated tiers to a base plus burst model. We'll share examples so sales can quickly price out deals.
[08:46] [09:00] Elena: Customer ask \u2014 better SSO/SAML docs and a support SLA for onboarding. We'll add a dedicated onboarding engineer to large accounts for the first 90 days.
[09:15] [09:30] Quick demos: Jordan showed a short screen-share of the new per-route tracing view (described verbally in transcript). There was a minor audio hiccup, some words mis-transcribed like "per-route trace" becoming "pear route brace" in the automated notes.
[09:54] Priya: Product will create a one-pager for the new tracing view and how to interpret the token-level cost waterfall.
[10:05] Maya: Closing remarks \u2014 iterate faster on Private quality, make Dedicated easier to buy, and double-down on observability and cost tooling.
[10:18] Maya: Thank you. We'll do a short AMA \u2014 drop questions in the #all-hands channel if we didn't get to them.
[10:30] AMA: (15 minutes) - assorted questions about PTO, remote-first policy, global expansions. A few answers were abbreviated; one comment mis-transcribed names and acronyms.
[11:10] Recap & Next steps: Maya read the top-level three priorities: 1) Ship Private bug fixes and improve onboarding (owner: Jordan), 2) Publish Dedicated SLA & pricing (owner: Priya), 3) Hire prioritized reliability engineers (owner: People Ops + Liam).
[11:34] Closing: meeting ends ~11:12 PST.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had medium quality \u2014 certain technical terms (KV cache, KMS, HSM) sometimes mis-transcribed; speaker boundaries occasionally merged. Refer to the recorded video for exact code names.
